Rolex · ref. 126333

Datejust

Dress/everyday · 36mm, 41mm (historic sizes varied) · 100m / 330ft · automatic · 1959–2026

The Rolex Datejust is a versatile, self-winding chronometer defined by its iconic date window at 3 o'clock, often magnified by a 'Cyclops' lens. It was the world's first wristwatch to feature an automatically changing date on the dial, establishing a standard for dress and everyday watches.

The story

Launched in 1945 to celebrate Rolex's 40th anniversary, the first Datejust (Ref. 4467) was available only in yellow gold and introduced the Jubilee bracelet. Key innovations followed, including the signature Cyclops magnifying lens in the 1950s and an instantaneous date change mechanism. The late 1970s brought the Caliber 3035, which introduced a high-beat movement and a convenient quickset date feature. In 1988, the highly successful Caliber 3135 was introduced, powering the Datejust for decades and coinciding with the switch from acrylic to scratch-resistant sapphire crystals. To meet modern demand for larger sizes, Rolex introduced the 41mm Datejust II in 2009, which was later refined and replaced by the current Datejust 41 in 2016 with an updated movement.
